findings: Frontal (AP) digital subtraction-type abdominal aortogram with a catheter tip in the upper abdominal aorta, projected at about the celiac/SMA level, and contrast opacifying the aorta, renal arteries and iliac arteries.
The right renal artery has a beaded, alternating stenosis and dilatation pattern (string-of-beads) in its mid to distal segment, before it branches within the kidney.
The left renal artery is smooth and of normal caliber, with normal intrarenal branching and a normal nephrogram.
The right kidney shows a preserved arterial tree and cortical blush, with no definite infarct or occlusion.
The abdominal aorta is smooth and of normal caliber, with no aneurysm or significant stenosis, and it bifurcates into the common iliac arteries that continue into the pelvis.
A large lucent gas-filled stomach or bowel structure lies in the left upper abdomen, with additional gas-filled bowel loops in both lower quadrants, and the lumbar spine is faintly seen.
Exposure and brightness are uneven, with a bright, overexposed right lateral edge.
differential: Fibromuscular dysplasia (medial fibroplasia) of the right renal artery
Segmental arterial mediolysis or renal artery vasculitis
Atherosclerotic renal artery disease (less likely given the classic beaded morphology and the smooth aorta)
anatomyConcerns: No impossible anatomy is seen; the renal arteries, aorta and iliac bifurcation follow a normal configuration.
The beaded right renal artery is a genuine vascular finding rather than an anatomical impossibility or artifact.
The uneven exposure at the right edge and the overlying bowel gas are acquisition features and do not indicate pathology.

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The right renal artery shows a classic string-of-beads pattern of alternating short stenoses and round dilatations in its mid to distal segment, with a normal origin. The left renal artery, the aorta and the intrarenal branching are smooth and normal. This pattern with hypertension and headaches in a young adult favors renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia (medial fibroplasia). Vasculitis and segmental arterial mediolysis are less likely because the beading is classic and there are no aneurysms, occlusions or infarcts. Atherosclerosis is unlikely given the smooth aorta and the normal origin. The uneven exposure at the right edge and the overlying bowel gas are acquisition features. There is a single gas-filled stomach bubble, continuous bowel loops, two kidneys, a faint midline lumbar spine and a flush catheter in the aorta, so there are no anatomical impossibilities. The image has no lettering.

clueFacts.fact: Renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia can cause renovascular hypertension, and headaches are a common symptom of that raised blood pressure; FMD can also involve the arteries to the brain.
